title: Email masking runs in linear time on long unbroken text

change.what: The two email replaces in redactPrivateText (the @ form and the [at]/(at) form) now run through maskEmails: the same two patterns, made sticky, tried only at the previous match end or where a run of [A-Z0-9._%+-] (case-insensitive) starts; run starts are found with the lookbehind (?<![A-Z0-9._%+-]).
change.whyNotLookbehindAlone: A lookbehind inside the pattern also blocks the position where the previous match ended, which a global replace tries. Measured on the old code against lookbehind-only: 'a@b.co-x@y.org' old '[redacted email][redacted email]', lookbehind-only '[redacted email]-x@y.org'; 'x [at] y [dot] com_z [at] w [dot] org' leaked '_z [at] w [dot] org' the same way. maskEmails keeps that start, so nothing is loosened.
change.unchanged: Patterns, flags, replacement text, the order (numbers, PAN, phone, @ form, [at] form, labels) and every other rule.

equalityArgument: Let L = [A-Z0-9._%+-] with the i flag. Both patterns begin with L+ and the next required character is not in L: '@' for the first; whitespace, '[' or '(' for the second.

So from any start s inside a run of L that ends at r, L+ can only stop at r: stopping at k < r would need text[k] to be '@', whitespace, '[' or '(', but text[k] is in L. Every start in the run therefore has the same continuation from r, and succeeds or fails exactly as the run start does.

A global replace tries positions left to right from the previous match end e. Inside the run that contains e, the first position it tries is e itself; in every later run, the first is the run start. A start whose character is not in L fails at once. So the first match it finds always starts at e or at a run start, and maskEmails tries exactly those positions in the same order with the same pattern.
Neither pattern can match the empty string, so both continue from the match end the same way.

benchmark.shape: redactPrivateText on one unbroken token of 'a' (no @), single call, this PC, Node 24.19.0

otherPatternsAt64KiB.note: Whole redactPrivateText after the change, so email time is excluded. Before the change each of these shapes took 16.6 to 18.4 s, all of it in the email scan.

notFixed.where: redact.ts maskJsonNumberTokens, reached through redactDerivative for strings starting with '[' or '{'
notFixed.shape: Not a regex start-anchoring problem: at every digit after a failed end-boundary check it runs the anchored number regex on text.slice(index), rescanning the digit run

tests.linear: Four 64 KiB tokens of 'aB3._%+-' (no @; spaces near the end; ' [at] ' near the end; '@' near the end), one timed call each, each under 100 ms (whole test 6.7 to 11.8 ms). On the old code this test fails at 16254 ms.
tests.equal: redactPrivateText compared with a copy of the old function on 25 hand-picked and 2000 seeded generated test_only strings: all 2025 equal, 967 changed by some masking, at least 200 contain [redacted email] (asserted). The two consecutive-match counterexamples are asserted to mask both addresses.
